g.text: Figure 3. Which layers are fragile, and what Stage 1 is told to do

text.style: font-size: 9px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #444444

g.text: Stage 0 run 20261003-144910_3df5df (same on Colab, 20261004-120724_3c2a04), TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat (22 layers, 1.10 B parameters, 2.20 GB at 16 bits)
Bar colours show our method: all 11 blue layers keep 8 bits and lose nothing, and the rest get 4 bits with 30% removed.

Higher score = more fragile layer; for size, smaller is better. The score is the layer's rank by damage, not the damage itself: the five 'never pruned' layers are where removing one layer hurts by far the most. Sizes are predictions that count 1 bit per weight to mark which weights were removed.
Our method, protected: 8 bits, nothing removed (11 layers)
Our method, compressed: 4 bits, 30% removed (11 layers)
Never pruned in any plan (the guard, from layer removal)
